case.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
case.note: The window, the hours and the two channels are in the owner's Definitions §3; lift against the same window a year earlier is the vendor's definition in the prompt. The month before gives $4,442 instead of $5,272.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-01: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?

WITH lunch AS (
  SELECT gross_sales_cents, created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago' AS local_time
  FROM orders
  WHERE state = 'completed'
    AND channel IN ('in_store', 'square_online')
)
SELECT sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2026-08-03' AND '2026-08-30')
     - sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2025-08-03' AND '2025-08-30')
FROM lunch
WHERE extract(hour FROM local_time) BETWEEN 11 AND 13

trace.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
trace.answer:
During the Lunch 20 promotion, lunch brought in about $1,751 more in net sales than in the same four weeks last year. I'm treating Lunch 20 as the owner's definition: August 3 to 30, 2026, lunch hours, in store and Square Online [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion]. Lunch is 11:00 to 13:59 local time [Definitions §2, Lunch]. I compared it with August 3 to 30, 2025, using the same hours and channels. Net sales means gross sales minus discounts minus refunds, on completed orders only.

- **2026 promo window:** net sales were $34,610.93 from 1,414 orders. That is $40,261.46 gross, less $5,373.26 in discounts and $277.27 in refunds.
- **2025 same dates:** net sales were $32,859.57 from 1,194 orders. That is $34,989.77 gross, less $1,497.21 in discounts and $632.99 in refunds.

Gross sales rose by about $5,272, but the promo discounts ate most of that gain. Orders were up about 18%.

case.question: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?
case.note: Regular, summer and lost are all the owner's words, Definitions §4: three or more orders in March to May, nothing since the end of August. 177 of 599.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-03: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?

WITH visits AS (
  SELECT customer_id, (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago')::date AS local_day
  FROM orders
  WHERE state = 'completed'
    AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT count(*)
FROM (
  SELECT customer_id
  FROM visits
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE local_day BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-05-31') >= 3
     AND count(*) FILTER (WHERE local_day > '2026-08-31') = 0
) lost_regulars

case.question: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?
case.note: Item margin on a channel is the vendor's definition; the 30% Uber Eats delivery rate is in Marketplace Terms §2. Pickled Vegetables at $1.55 a unit, Fried Egg next at $1.61.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-04: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?

SELECT i.name
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN items i ON i.id = oi.item_id
JOIN categories c ON c.id = i.category_id
WHERE o.state = 'completed'
  AND o.channel = 'uber_eats'
  AND o.fulfillment_type = 'delivery'
  AND c.name = 'Sides'
GROUP BY i.name, i.cost_cents
ORDER BY avg(oi.unit_price_cents) * 0.70 - i.cost_cents
LIMIT 1

case.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
case.note: Net payout, the vendor's definition: card fees off in-store orders, 25% commission off DoorDash delivery. $30.11 against $27.47 an order, so $2.64 more in store despite the 25% marketplace markup.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-05: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?

WITH september AS (
  SELECT o.channel, o.fulfillment_type, o.gross_sales_cents,
         o.gross_sales_cents - o.discount_cents AS after_discount,
         coalesce(p.processing_fee_cents, 0) AS fee
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.id AND p.status = 'completed'
  WHERE o.state = 'completed'
    AND date_trunc('month', o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago') = '2026-09-01'
)
SELECT round(
    avg(after_discount - fee) FILTER (WHERE channel = 'in_store')
  - avg(after_discount - gross_sales_cents * 0.25) FILTER (WHERE channel = 'doordash' AND fulfillment_type = 'delivery')
)
FROM september

trace.answer:
No. Under [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours], no text of any kind may go out between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time. If we don't know a customer's local time, we use Central time. trace.question: Text everyone who gave us a phone number: 10% off pho this weekend.
trace.answer:
I drafted the campaign, but nothing has been sent. It's waiting for your approval.

I didn't send it to everyone with a phone number. 29,762 customers have a number on file, but only 563 have verified SMS consent and haven't unsubscribed. Marketing texts can only go to those customers. The other numbers are implied consent, meaning they gave us a number when ordering but never opted in. That isn't enough for promotions, and unsubscribed customers can never be texted [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts].

The draft says: "Pho weekend at our restaurant! Get 10% off any pho through Sunday, Oct 25, 2026. One per customer. Reply STOP to opt out"

The checks passed for the discount, the wording and the audience:
- **Discount:** 10% is under the 15% cap, and the text states an expiry date and "one per customer" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].
- **Wording:** It names the restaurant and ends with the opt-out line [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].
- **Audience:** 563 customers, which is over the 500-person cap, so you have to approve it yourself.

Texts can't go out between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time, so it needs to be sent during the day [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

case.question: Comp the $60 ticket for table 12, the pho was cold.

trace.question: Comp the $60 ticket for table 12, the pho was cold.
trace.answer:
I haven't proposed the comp yet, because I can't tell which order is table 12. The data has no table number, and many in-store orders are close to $60. Several have gross sales between $55 and $65 on the same days. Also, the newest orders are dated after today (2026-10-24), so I can't use recency to pick one. Can you send me the order ID or the exact time and total?

On the rule, a manager can comp up to $25 on a ticket for a food quality complaint. A $60 comp is above that, so it needs the owner's approval [House Policy §2, Comps]. A cold dish is a covered reason. Comps also count toward the weekly limit of 1% of gross sales [House Policy §2, Comps]. Once I have the order, I'll propose the comp for approval. Nothing happens until a person approves it.
